segments.narration: An island invented writing and then forgot it. Rapa Nui, the Pacific. Two dozen carved wooden tablets survive.
The glyphs are tiny, carved with obsidian or shark teeth into hard driftwood, and packed edge to edge.
They run in reverse boustrophedon. You read a line, then physically rotate the tablet to read the next one.
By the eighteen seventies the people who could read them were gone, taken by slave raids and epidemics.
One sequence has been cracked: a lunar calendar on a tablet called Mamari. Everything else is still silent.
